hypotheses.claim: Executing pull-request merge code on a persistent self-hosted runner with persist-credentials=true creates an avoidable credential-bearing authority edge and residue risk.
hypotheses.test: Repeat on a disposable runner generation with least GITHUB_TOKEN permissions, persist-credentials=false, pre/post filesystem and credential-helper attestations, and an adversarial probe that attempts cross-step and next-job recovery.
hypotheses.falsifier: No credential or residue is recoverable across adversarial trials, cleanup receipts are complete, and equivalent authority is proven necessary for the workload.

hypotheses.claim: Typed gate failures prevent false transfer of one red status across instrument, semantic, test, benchmark, and host-trust layers.
hypotheses.test: Emit a signed layer vector for each job and compare triage accuracy and time-to-remediation against the untyped single-red baseline.
hypotheses.falsifier: Layer typing does not improve diagnosis or causes contradictory promotion decisions under the same receipts.

hypotheses.claim: A guard fix on main does not repair required-check evidence for an older PR head until that head incorporates the fix and reruns.
hypotheses.test: Select stale PR heads, record head SHA/check suites, merge or rebase the fix, rerun, and require receipts anchored to the new head SHA.
hypotheses.falsifier: A required check for an unchanged old head is legitimately replaced by the main-only result under repository rules.

counterhypotheses.claim: Runner availability plus passing unit tests is sufficient for a green gate.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: 28 tests passed, but the job failed at benchmark import.

counterhypotheses.claim: persist-credentials=true adds no meaningful authority exposure on a persistent PR lane.
counterhypotheses.counterevidence: Official GitHub guidance warns that persistent self-hosted runners may be compromised by untrusted workflow code; checkout documents credential persistence for later steps.

new_concepts.name: Execution Depth Vector
new_concepts.definition: A non-collapsible receipt vector: runner, checkout, tests, benchmark, whole-job, promotion.

new_concepts.name: Credential-Bearing PR Lane
new_concepts.definition: A workflow lane where untrusted PR-derived code and repository credentials coexist on non-ephemeral infrastructure.

new_concepts.name: Main-Fix Nonretroactivity
new_concepts.definition: A main-branch repair has no evidentiary effect on an older head until the tested SHA contains the repair.

new_concepts.name: Imported Receipt Lineage
new_concepts.definition: Imported work reports retain the actor and upstream execution lineage and do not become independent evidence through ingestion.
